Attack: how long the sound takes to fade in from silence to full volume.
Decay: how long it takes to fall from full volume to the sustain level.
How long the sound lasts, in seconds.
How long the audition note is held, in seconds.
Noise mix: blends a layer of hiss under the tone. Zero is a clean tone.
How high the sound ends. Lower than the start slides down; higher slides up.
How high the sound starts, in hertz (Hz). Higher numbers are higher notes.
Pulse width: 50% is a plain square wave; lower or higher values make a thinner, buzzier tone.
Release: how long the sound takes to fade out at the end.
Sustain: the volume held after the decay, as a share of full volume.
Fine tune: shifts every note up or down in cents (100 cents = one semitone).
How loud the sound is. A safe limit is always applied.
The character of the tone: Square is buzzy and retro, Triangle is soft, Saw is bright, Sine is pure, Noise is hiss and crash.
